level: actual default-product AgentLoop container-command acceptance on non-container and real-Docker hosts
implementation: grantFor now publishes remote/container_command_v1 only for workspace-write scopes that also include operation_status and operation_cancel; the backend is no longer registered without the corresponding Bot capability.
The default product probe expects all four managed backends (mr-api, codex-read, remote-write and remote-command) and drives the real AgentLoop through bot_task_start with a fixed argv alias.

The plain-Agent branch proves never-started, possiblyApplied:false, confirmed stop and no workspace lock. The real-Docker branch proves exitCode 0, possiblyApplied:true, confirmed stop, one original operation and no retained lock.
preservedFailures: The first default-product run failed with TOOL_DENIED because grantFor did not publish remote/container_command_v1 even though the backend was registered. The grant compiler was fixed; no authorization was bypassed.
The next assertion initially read the journal summary instead of the public remote projection. The probe was corrected to assert result.code and result.remote rather than changing the task contract.

The first minimal remote fixture attempts failed before product execution because integration-upstream-tests, integration-combined-host, task-executors and official-tool-executor modules were absent. A fresh complete-source directory and existing isolated dependency links were used instead of hiding those environment failures.

One full-root run also hit a transient Windows EPERM rename in migration-configuration-commit. The focused suite then passed 12/12 and the final full rerun completed with zero failures; the original record was not rewritten.
observed: The default product now exposes all four backends and compiles the command capability into the same Bot grant used by the actual AgentLoop submission.
Win11 completes all 42 default-product checks, including the non-container never-started command path with no native fallback and no retained workspace lock.
Ubuntu completes all 42 default-product checks with the real fixed container image: the approved node alias runs once, returns exitCode 0 and produces confirmed stop evidence.
Final local root regression has 1853 tests, 1785 pass, 0 fail and 68 explicit skips. check:client and integration:check pass. No real model request or user profile write occurred.
limitations: The remote run reused existing isolated dependencies; it is not a clean-install or production deployment proof. The complete-source archive and the focused overlay hashes are recorded separately.
Command exposure remains limited to the approved workspace-write/container binding and argv aliases. Broader model-facing command policy and Windows OS-isolated commands remain open.
This does not close stop-fence slices 4/5, real inference/billing, migration activation, production sleep/topology or full package acceptance.
